profile.name: Golam Wasy
profile.roleLine: Backend-first, full-stack capable. Building reliable systems and tools people actually rely on.

bio.whoami: Software Engineer, mostly backend with Java and Spring Boot, and comfortable on the frontend with React and TypeScript. I care about reliable, well tested code, and I support what I ship in production. My Master's research on anomaly detection taught me to dig into a problem properly before building.
bio.mission: Turning complex business requirements into working software. REST APIs across microservices with Kafka and PostgreSQL on the backend, React and TypeScript on the frontend, with JUnit, Mockito, contract tests and Playwright to keep it honest, and CI/CD, Docker and on-call to keep it running.

experiences.desc: Built internal apps for post-sale work: customer accounts, support, invoices, refunds and sale adjustments. Built and maintained a refund and reallocation system with multiple payments, approvals and audit logging, and developed Spring Boot REST APIs for sale and tax adjustments with permission-based approval flows, across microservices talking over REST and Kafka. Moved heavy data processing to the backend with efficient pagination and search, shipped behind LaunchDarkly flags and Drools rules, fixed Snyk vulnerabilities and upgraded services to a new major Spring Boot version. On the frontend, redesigned Retool apps and helped plan and start the migration to React and TypeScript, with Playwright tests. Deployed through CircleCI, debugged with Honeycomb and was part of the monthly on-call rotation.

Evaluated how adaptive normalization techniques affect the accuracy of anomaly detection models. Built data processing services in Python and FastAPI to run the evaluations, and compared models implemented in PyTorch and TensorFlow on real-world time series data from telecommunications networks and IoT sensors.

experiences.company: University of Helsinki & Nokia Bell Labs
experiences.desc: Joint research project on data efficiency techniques for mobile networks, with the Network Systems and Security Research Lab and Nokia's Network Operation department. Built the research foundation for my thesis: studied adaptive normalization techniques, evaluated datasets and worked with real mobile network data, including incomplete transmissions.

Freelance work on client projects across backend, web and mobile. Built REST APIs in Java and Spring Boot with PostgreSQL and implemented JWT authentication for a client. Extended an Angular admin console, built a customer feedback feature in an Ionic app from UI to backend, and integrated Google Maps to show car dealer locations. Worked directly with enterprise clients on requirements.

My first proper backend role. Integrated APIs with Spring Boot, wrote MySQL migration scripts and Java unit tests before work reached client servers, and deployed applications to client servers on AWS in an agile team using Git, Jira and Confluence.

projects.name: Clearpath
projects.description: Distributed platform with Kotlin/Ktor services, a Go service and a TypeScript/React web app, using PostgreSQL, Redis, MongoDB and Kafka on Docker and Kubernetes. Built by directing an AI agent, with the service boundaries, data invariants and tests designed and reviewed by me. Self-hosted on my own Linux server.

projects.name: Planora
projects.description: AI-assisted project planning tool with an LLM-powered risk assessment feature. The model's output is shown alongside the reasoning behind it, so users can tell when to trust it and when to check it themselves.

projects.name: Portfolio
projects.description: This site. Terminal-themed portfolio built with Next.js 16 and React 19, with content served from Redis and self-hosted with Docker Compose behind Traefik on my own server, deployed by GitHub Actions.
